role: TTAB Administrative Trademark Judge (or panel) writing a decision in a contested inter partes proceeding (opposition, cancellation, concurrent use, or interference) under the Lanham Act, evaluating likelihood-of-confusion (DuPont factors), priority, distinctiveness/descriptiveness, abandonment, dilution, fraud, and related registrability or registration-maintenance grounds
target: a contested trademark registration or registrability claim — including the applicant's mark sought to be registered (opposition), the respondent's already-issued registration sought to be cancelled (cancellation), or the parties' competing marks and territorial rights (concurrent use / interference) — and the parties' arguments and evidence directed at those claims
inline_evidence_example: the phrase "the marks share an identical first syllable, COR-, which is the dominant feature consumers will recall in the marketplace under the second DuPont factor" is an observation that evidences a 'mark-similarity-first-syllable-dominance' norm without naming the norm; the phrase "Opposer's evidence of single use a year does not establish priority of use sufficient to give it standing under Section 1063" is a complaint that evidences a 'priority-of-use-bona-fide-use' norm; the phrase "the very nature of the charge of fraud requires that it be proven 'to the hilt' with clear and convincing evidence" is an observation that evidences a 'fraud-clear-and-convincing-burden' norm anchored to In re Bose; the phrase "a term is deemed to be merely descriptive of goods or services, within the meaning of Section 2(e)(1), if it forthwith conveys an immediate idea of an ingredient, quality, characteristic, feature, function, purpose or use of the goods or services" is a suggestion that evidences a 'mere-descriptiveness-immediate-idea' norm (the Marvin Ginn / Gyulay formulation); the phrase "a strong mark such as Opposer's 'casts a long shadow which competitors must avoid'" is praise that evidences a 'fame-broad-scope-of-protection' norm; the phrase "Petitioner has not prosecuted this case as a traditional abandonment case" used to justify reframing the claim under the abandonment standard is a complaint that evidences a 'pleading-construed-by-substance-not-label' norm. Counter-examples — these are NOT norm signals: the case caption (party names, proceeding number, judges' names, counsel) — caption / boilerplate has no norm content; "International Class 25" or "Application Serial No. 87902522" — bare identifiers; "Mailed: August 25, 2021" or a TTABVUE citation pin alone ("26 TTABVUE 9"); a footnote that is purely a record citation with no doctrinal move. Bare procedural recitations (who filed what when, the list of witnesses, the list of exhibits, the list of evidentiary objections without ruling) emit ZERO signals unless the Board is using them to make a doctrinal point.
polarity_hint:
TTAB inter partes decisions are JUDICIAL OPINIONS by a panel of Administrative Trademark Judges — the voice is formal, third-person plural ("we find", "we focus", "the Board concludes"), and DOMINATED BY REASONING-MOVES (observation and suggestion) rather than complaint or praise. The dense norm-bearing moves are: (i) STANDING / ENTITLEMENT (Section 13/14, Lexmark zone-of-interests + proximate-cause, real interest beyond mere intermeddler, registrations as basis for standing); (ii) PRIORITY (constructive use date = filing date, common-law use, analogous use, the King Candy presumption when no counterclaim); (iii) the THIRTEEN DUPONT FACTORS for Section 2(d) likelihood of confusion — particularly: similarity of the marks in appearance/sound/connotation/commercial impression (factor 1, Palm Bay), similarity and nature of the goods/services (factor 2), similarity of channels of trade (factor 3), conditions of purchase / sophistication of buyers (factor 4), fame of the prior mark (factor 5, Bose Corp.), number and nature of similar marks in use on similar goods (factor 6, third-party use), nature and extent of any actual confusion (factor 7), length of concurrent use without confusion (factor 8), variety of goods on which the mark is used / scope of the prior mark (factor 9), and market interface between applicant and prior user (factor 10); related sub-norms include the doctrine of legal identity of goods, presumption of overlapping trade channels when goods are identical (Viterra), the anti-dissection rule combined with attention to dominant features (National Data, Detroit Athletic), the descriptive-portion-given-less-weight rule (Dixie Restaurants), and the rule that the verbal portion of a word-and-design composite is usually dominant (Viterra) with explicit case-specific exceptions; (iv) DISTINCTIVENESS / DESCRIPTIVENESS UNDER Section 2(e) — the Gyulay / Abcor immediate-idea test, the Marvin Ginn genericness primary-significance test, suggestive-vs-descriptive imagination-thought-and-perception line (MBNA), composite-mark unitary-meaning rule (Colonial Stores), the "someone who knows what the goods are" framing (Tower Tech), acquired distinctiveness / secondary meaning under Section 2(f); (v) ABANDONMENT under Section 45 / 1127 — discontinuance + intent not to resume, three-consecutive-years presumption, bona fide use in the ordinary course of trade (not made merely to reserve a right in a mark), preponderance of the evidence burden (Cerveceria Centroamericana, Imperial Tobacco); (vi) FRAUD under In re Bose Corp. (Fed. Cir. 2009) — "to the hilt" / clear-and-convincing standard, knowing materially-false representation, subjective intent to deceive as indispensable element, replacing the prior Medinol "knew or should have known" standard; (vii) DILUTION under Section 43(c) — fame, distinctiveness, blurring/tarnishment; (viii) procedural and evidentiary norms — TTABVUE practice, Trademark Rule 2.122 incorporation of file history, notice of reliance under Rule 2.122(d)/(e), testimony deposition requirements, judicial notice of dictionary definitions, waiver of unpleaded affirmative defenses, the rule that pleadings must be construed by substance and not by label (when the Board reframes a poorly-pleaded claim under the correct doctrine), the rule that statements not raised in trial brief are waived. Praise is rare and almost always directed at a PARTY'S EVIDENCE the Board credits, at a PRIOR PANEL'S REASONING the Board adopts, or at a CITED FEDERAL CIRCUIT precedent the Board follows; complaint applies to a PARTY'S DEFICIENT EVIDENCE, a MISREADING OF THE STATUTE, a WAIVED CLAIM, a FAILURE TO MEET THE BURDEN OF PROOF, or an UNSUPPORTED ARGUMENT. Most signals are signal_type observation (declarative statements of doctrine and findings) or suggestion (prescriptive rules — "a party seeking cancellation must demonstrate ...", "the proper test is not a side-by-side comparison"). Where one party cites a precedent and the Board distinguishes or extends it, those signals are particularly norm-rich.

DATASET-SPECIFIC OVERRIDES (these REPLACE the generic constraints where they conflict):

(a) The input is a TTAB INTER PARTES DECISION (often truncated to 18,000 chars from the head of the opinion). Aim for HIGH RECALL across the WHOLE decision: 8-25 passages per decision is typical for substantive merits decisions covering multiple grounds. Each passage should be a doctrinally-coherent unit (a standing paragraph, a DuPont-factor paragraph, an abandonment-bona-fide-use paragraph, a fraud-burden paragraph, etc.) and not a sentence fragment. A standalone case citation with no surrounding reasoning is NOT a passage. A pure record-citation footnote ("26 TTABVUE 4 n.1") with no doctrinal proposition is NOT a passage.

(b) ATTRIBUTION RULE — signals must capture THE BOARD'S OWN reasoning, not the parties' arguments quoted in the decision. When the decision says "Opposer alleges", "Petitioner contends", "Applicant argues", "Respondent denies", that paraphrase of a party's position is NOT itself a signal — the signal is the Board's own move ACCEPTING, REJECTING, QUALIFYING, or RESTATING that argument. The clearest cues are the judicial voice: "the Board finds", "we find", "we conclude", "we focus", "we agree", "we are not persuaded", "Opposer's evidence does not establish", "Petitioner has failed to demonstrate", "This factor weighs heavily in favor of". Also acceptable as Board's voice are unattributed declarative statements of law that the Board is adopting ("A mark has been 'abandoned' [w]hen its use has been discontinued with intent not to resume such use.", "The party seeking cancellation based on abandonment bears the burden of proving its case by a preponderance of the evidence.") — these are the Board speaking in the doctrinal-exposition register.

(c) signal_type ENUM IS STRICTLY {complaint, praise, observation, suggestion}. (i) Most doctrinal statements ("A term is deemed to be merely descriptive of goods or services, within the meaning of Section 2(e)(1), if ...") are `observation` with polarity `neutral`, or `suggestion` when prescriptive about how a party MUST plead or prove. (ii) The Board rejecting a party's argument, finding the burden of proof unmet, or finding evidence insufficient is `complaint` with polarity `negative` (the complaint is directed AT the losing argument or insufficient evidence). (iii) The Board crediting a party's evidence, finding a registration entitled to broad scope of protection, finding a mark commercially strong, or adopting Federal Circuit reasoning is `praise` with polarity `positive`. (iv) Statements of how doctrine SHOULD apply in future / what a party MUST prove / what is REQUIRED to make out a claim or defense ("Petitioner must meet this burden by showing that, with respect to any particular identified good, the mark's 'use has been discontinued with intent not to resume such use.'") are `suggestion`. Use `suggestion` for prescriptive doctrinal statements that direct future conduct or set the test, not for descriptive ones.

(d) CITATION-INSIDE-PASSAGE: TTAB decisions are dense with citations to Federal Circuit, CCPA, Supreme Court, and TTAB precedents (e.g. "In re E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co., 476 F.2d 1357, 177 USPQ 563, 567 (CCPA 1973)", "Palm Bay Imps. Inc. v. Veuve Clicquot Ponsardin Maison Fondee En 1772, 396 F.3d 1369, 73 USPQ2d 1689, 1694 (Fed. Cir. 2005)", "In re Bose Corp., 476 F.3d 1331, 91 USPQ2d 1938 (Fed. Cir. 2009)", "Trademark Act Section 45, 15 U.S.C. § 1127"). These citations ARE part of the doctrinal move and SHOULD be kept inside the signal_text when the Board is invoking that authority for the proposition stated. They should NOT be a signal on their own. signal_text 10-200 char window includes the citation when natural.

(e) HIERARCHY OF AUTHORITY MATTERS AND IS ITSELF A NORM. The TTAB is bound by Federal Circuit decisions (which review TTAB appeals) and by Supreme Court decisions; CCPA decisions (the TTAB's pre-1982 reviewing court) are binding precedent; TTAB precedential decisions bind the Board; TTAB non-precedential decisions (most modern decisions) are persuasive only. When the Board explicitly notes a precedent's hierarchical position or invokes a controlling-vs-persuasive distinction, that hierarchical marker should be in signal_text.

(f) Bare procedural recitations (case caption, list of pending motions, identification of counsel, the proceeding number, the panel composition, the list of testimony depositions filed without ruling) emit ZERO signals. SKIP the case caption / boilerplate / footnote-record-citations. The STANDING / PRIORITY / SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS / CONCLUSION sections are where most signals live. Evidentiary-objection rulings DO emit signals when the Board states an evidentiary norm (e.g., waiver from untimely objection, the hearsay rule applied to in-house declarations).

(g) PRESERVE the source text VERBATIM in passage_text and signal_text. TTAB decisions are PDF-OCR-converted and contain artifacts: stray newlines mid-sentence, broken hyphenation ("de-scriptive"), spaces inserted inside words ("Comp any", "de fenses"), trailing whitespace, footnote markers as superscript digits or interpolated ("4", "5", "6" mid-text), section symbols (§§), em dashes (—), curly quotes (“ ” ‘ ’), and the persistent line-numbering header pattern "Opposition No. 91244445\n7\n" or "Cancellation No. 92056654\n8\n" between paragraphs. Copy character-for-character. Do not normalize, do not correct OCR errors, do not splice out the page-header noise — leave it where it appears in the source.

(h) When two or more discrete doctrinal moves appear in the same paragraph (e.g. the Board first states the burden of proof, then states the legal standard, then applies it to the facts), emit each as its own signal inside the same passage. 3-8 signals per substantive passage is typical for the dense doctrinal sections (DuPont analysis, fraud-burden recitation, abandonment standard).

(i) MULTI-GROUND DECISIONS are typical for inter partes proceedings: a single opposition may plead Section 2(d) likelihood of confusion, Section 2(e) descriptiveness, Section 43(c) dilution, and Section 14(3) abandonment all together; a cancellation may plead abandonment plus fraud. The decision then has DISTINCT SECTIONS for each ground. Emit passages spanning all such grounds — do not focus only on the dispositive ground. Even when one ground is waived or summarily denied, the Board's reasoning for the waiver/denial is itself a norm-bearing move (e.g., "Petitioner does not address its claim of fraud in its brief on the case ... We find that Petitioner has waived its claim of fraud.").
